headline: High: Continue’s filesystem/MCP tool access can create prompt-injection and data-leak paths, while godot_rl_agents adds little direct mitigation or overlap.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs could be treated as instructions. godot_rl_agents exposes no input surfaces or defenses, so it does not reduce the pathway. The pair is not proven to share a channel by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace files, prompt-like content in those files can influence Continue.
IF Continue is configured to consume MCP output as trusted text, injected instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Restrict Continue to a read-only workspace copy.
Disable or whitelist MCP servers for the session.
Separate the two agents onto different directories.
Add a manual review step before any tool-using action.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file and MCP content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can egress broadly to a user-chosen model provider, so sensitive workspace content may leave the host. godot_rl_agents shows no data classes or egress, so it is not the leak source. The pairwise risk is medium because the leakage path exists in default Continue-style use, but the second agent does not amplify it.
conditions: IF Continue is connected to a remote model provider, workspace content can be transmitted off-host.
IF the shared workspace contains secrets or proprietary code, those contents may be exposed in prompts or outputs.
mitigations: Use a local model provider for Continue.
Exclude secret-bearing directories from the workspace.
Open only the minimum files needed for the task.
Turn off broad network egress for the session.
requires-engineering: enforce content redaction before model calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but godot_rl_agents has no documented write, network, or mutable-resource capabilities. There is no evidence of overlapping write targets or shared mutable state beyond Continue’s own filesystem use, so direct capability conflict is limited and low.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents is extended to write shared files or git state, conflicts could emerge.
IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mutable directory, write contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep godot_rl_agents read-only relative to shared assets.
Run Continue in a separate working directory.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Use file locks for any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or file edits, but godot_rl_agents has no documented downstream action-taking authority and no evidence that it blindly trusts Continue’s outputs. Without a documented handoff, the cascade is possible only if an operator wires them together, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF outputs from Continue are copied into godot_rl_agents workflows without review, errors can cascade.
IF an operator treats Continue-generated code as authoritative, downstream mistakes may persist.
mitigations: Require human review of Continue outputs.
Do not auto-feed Continue outputs into downstream actions.
Test generated changes in a throwaway branch.
Keep godot_rl_agents isolated from code-editing workflows.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any automated action.

E_compliance.rationale: Continue handles source code and open editor buffers, which may include regulated or sensitive material, while godot_rl_agents documents no data classes or residency constraints. There is no explicit mismatch shown, but Continue’s broad egress means compliance gaps can arise if sensitive data is present and sent to a remote provider. The other agent is not the compliance driver.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Continue and sent to a remote model provider, policy violations may occur.
IF the workspace contains data subject to retention or residency rules, Continue’s egress can conflict with them.
mitigations: Use only non-sensitive files in Continue.
Prefer a local inference backend.
Document the data classes allowed in the workspace.
Review retention settings for the model provider.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data paths.
